structurally_unverifiable.reason: their source document prints imperial units only, with no metric equivalent to cross-check against. PERMANENT - collecting more text cannot raise it.

quarantine.note: Kept in the corpus, not the repo: it is a work queue, not a deliverable.

limitations: VERIFICATION IS A PROPERTY OF THE DOCUMENT, NOT THE UNIT, AND THE CEILING IS PERMANENT. 36 CFR 1191 prints every dimension twice and verifies at 258/261 = 98.9%. OSHA (29 CFR 1910, 1926) and HUD (24 CFR 3280) print imperial only and verify at 7/311 = 2.3% - in BOTH units. So 311 of 572 rules (54.4%) are STRUCTURALLY unverifiable by the dual-unit cross-check: their source prints no metric equivalent, and no amount of further collecting can raise that. It is a structural ceiling, not a sample-size problem. The per-unit figures (in 60%, ft 4.3%) are themselves an aggregate hiding this - feet look unverifiable only because 132 of the 140 foot rules come from imperial-only documents; inside 36 CFR 1191 feet verify at 4/5. Practical consequence for a consumer: treat 36 CFR 1191 rules as cross-checked and every other document's rules as parsed-but-unconfirmed, and weight a compliance finding accordingly.

COVERAGE, MEASURED 2026-08-27 (not estimated): the eCFR search API reports 2,957 sections CFR-wide carrying the dual-unit dimensional pattern, across 230 parts, with count relation 'eq' (not a capped 'gte'). The 7 parts harvested here hold 185 of them = 6.3%. BUT that denominator is dimensional prose in general, not building rules - the largest holders are fisheries (50 CFR 648), endangered species, hazmat shipping and consumer appliances. Filtering the 223 unharvested parts by building-related headings leaves 23 parts / 148 sections, and most of those are vehicles (46 CFR vessel construction, 49 CFR 38 and 36 CFR 1192 transportation) or nuclear (10 CFR 50). Genuinely building-relevant and still missing: 28 CFR 36 (DOJ ADA Title III), 36 CFR 1190 (PROWAG, public right-of-way), 36 CFR 1234 (records storage facilities), 16 CFR 1211 (residential garage door operators), 7 CFR 1924 (construction and repair). So coverage of BUILDING dimensional CFR is high, and 6.3% understates it - but the honest figure is 'high', not 'complete', and the remaining candidates are named above rather than left as an unbounded gap.

eCFR XML only. UFC and ADA PDFs are NOT parsed - they carry no machine-readable section tree, so any citation from them would be reconstructed rather than sourced. That is 169 UFC PDFs (679 MB) and 2 ADA PDFs whose rule content is entirely unmeasured - unlike the CFR gap above, this one has NO number attached to it yet.
Subject extraction is shallow (text before 'shall'). Every rule carries its verbatim quote so a human can check what was read.
Applicability/scope is NOT modelled. A rule knows its section and heading, not which building types or occupancies it governs.
Permissive, conditional and exception clauses are quarantined, not interpreted. Some of them ARE requirements under conditions.
No rule here has been evaluated against a real reconstructed plan.
